literal: Enduring the pain that comes upon oneself, and not doing harm to other lives, is indeed of that nature which is the true form of penance.
translation: To endure the suffering that comes upon oneself and to refrain from causing harm to any living being—this is the true form of penance.
modern: தனக்கு வரும் துன்பங்களைப் பொறுத்துக் கொள்வதும், பிற உயிர்களுக்குத் துன்பம் செய்யாமல் இருப்பதுமே தவத்தின் உண்மையான வடிவமாகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines the true nature and form of penance (தவம்). It consists of two essential aspects: first, 'நோன்றல்' (enduring) the 'உற்றநோய்' (pain or hardships that come upon oneself), and second, 'செய்யாமை' (not doing) 'உறுகண்' (harm or distress) to any 'உயிர்க்கு' (living being). The word 'உரு' here means the true form or essence, indicating that penance is not merely an external ritual but an internal discipline of patience and non-violence. Together, these two practices constitute the complete definition of ascetic virtue.
